introduction: On this seventh Sunday of Easter, between the Ascension and Pentecost, the apostles gather in the upper room and devote themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus. In the Gospel, Jesus prays to the Father for his disciples: This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God. Peter tells us to rejoice when we share in Christ's sufferings. Let us pray with Mary for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the disciples prayed with Mary for the coming of the Spirit. Let us join our prayers to theirs.
intentions: For the Church: that, gathered in prayer like the first disciples, she may be ready to receive the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians who suffer for the name of Christ: that the Spirit of glory may rest on them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are seeking God: that they may come to know him, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom he sent. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our families and communities: that we may pray together with one heart, as the disciples did with Mary. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may know God and live eternal life even now. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Holy Father, your Son prayed for his disciples before he returned to you. Hear his prayer for us, and send us your Holy Spirit, so that we may know you and glorify you. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: With Mary, in prayer
reflection.body:
After the Ascension, the apostles return to Jerusalem and go to the upper room. Luke lists them by name, and then tells us what they did: "All these with one accord continued steadfastly in prayer and supplication, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus." Christians have long seen in these days the first novena: nine days of prayer, waiting for the Holy Spirit. And Mary is at the heart of it, as she was at the beginning of Jesus' life.

In the Gospel, we listen to Jesus himself praying at the Last Supper. He lifts his eyes to heaven: "Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you." Then he tells us what eternal life is: "This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ." Eternal life is not only life after death; it is knowing God, a relationship that begins now.

Jesus prays for his disciples, who will stay behind in the world: "I pray for them... for they are yours." He knows they will face difficulties: "I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you."

Peter speaks to Christians who are suffering for their faith. He tells them not to be surprised but to rejoice, "because you are partakers of Christ's sufferings." And if they are insulted for the name of Christ, "you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you."

This week, between the Ascension and Pentecost, do what the first disciples did: pray, with Mary, for the Holy Spirit. Perhaps pray a decade of the Rosary each day for a new outpouring of the Spirit on the Church and on your family.
